title: chore: the postflight fake-proxy twins have diverged; reconcile them or pin their intentional differences
description:
Found 2026-10-25 by worker-9cda703c (task-e92b2cb3, step 1); see mem gotcha-postflight-fake-proxy-twins-diverged.

**The divergence.** The fake-proxy JavaScript embedded in scripts/tests/postflight.sh (the `cat > "$FAKE_PROXY" <<'JS'` heredoc) and in scripts/tests/postflight.ps1 (the `Set-Content -Path $fakeProxy -Encoding UTF8 -Value @'` here-string) is NOT byte-identical. Measured at HEAD b35d46c, after normalizing UTF-8 BOM and CRLF:
- cmp exit 1, first difference at byte 663, line 17;
- lengths 32746 (sh) vs 31418 (ps1);
- SHA-256 7c3afb75… (sh) vs caf7a0b0… (ps1).

The first difference is the ps1-only readTask/strList/declaredSets/csv helpers. Resume status, blocked task id/nextAction and get_commit_scope logic differ too. The integration squash 5e74fb8 already differed (28787 vs 27979), so peer edits are not the cause.

**Why it matters:**
- docs/DEVELOPMENT.md says both smoke tests "verify the same contract through a fake proxy".
- task-e92b2cb3's rail assumed the twins are byte-identical "as the surrounding cases already require".
Neither claim holds, nothing checks it, and differing fixtures can hide wrapper parity bugs.

**Work:**
1. Classify every difference: shared contract (harmonize it) or engine-specific (keep it, with a comment at the site saying why).
2. Add an automated check that fails when the shared part drifts, for example a parity-check group that extracts both bodies and compares them.
3. Preserve each platform's fixture requirements. Never copy one proxy wholesale over the other.

**Serialization:** postflight.{sh,ps1} are also planned or edited by task-5f3960df, task-07474ee4 and task-c2cb5cf7. Whoever plans this row must set dependsOn against them, per the overlap rail.
definitionOfDone: Every difference between the extracted sh and ps1 fake-proxy bodies is either removed or marked at its site as engine-specific, with the reason.
An automated check in both parity checkers (or one they share) fails when the shared fake-proxy part drifts, proven RED on a scratch copy with one injected difference.
MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180 bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh and postflight.ps1 (PS 5.1 and pwsh 7) pass from a HEAD snapshot, and parity-check.sh and parity-check.ps1 stay green.
docs/DEVELOPMENT.md's fake-proxy sentence matches the result.
taskRails: Harness, parity-checker and docs changes only: scripts/moe-agent.sh and scripts/moe-agent.ps1 stay unchanged unless a harmonized fixture proves a wrapper wrong, which becomes its own bug row.

implementationPlan.description:
Parity group first (RED on today's tree).

Add a 'postflight fake proxy' group to BOTH scripts/tests/parity-check.sh and scripts/tests/parity-check.ps1. Each uses its own native implementation, as the existing groups do. The group passes only when all three hold:
- (a) scripts/tests/postflight-fake-proxy.js exists.
- (b) scripts/tests/postflight.sh INSTALLS it: a `cp` of postflight-fake-proxy.js to "$FAKE_PROXY". Match the install line itself, not any mention, and require that no `cat > "$FAKE_PROXY" <<` heredoc remains.
- (c) scripts/tests/postflight.ps1 installs it with a `Copy-Item` of postflight-fake-proxy.js to $fakeProxy, and no `Set-Content -Path $fakeProxy` here-string remains.

Error handling: each failure prints a PARITY FAIL line naming the harness and what drifted, and counts toward the checker's existing failure total. A missing file is a failure, never a silent skip.

Run both checkers now. They must FAIL on today's tree, because both harnesses embed private proxy bodies. That run is this task's test that fails on the old behaviour (epic rail). Update each checker's header comment to name the new group.

The ps1 harness installs the shared proxy, and the docs say so.

In scripts/tests/postflight.ps1, delete the fake-proxy here-string and install the shared file instead: `Copy-Item -LiteralPath (Join-Path <repo root> 'scripts\tests\postflight-fake-proxy.js') -Destination $fakeProxy -ErrorAction Stop`, using the harness's existing root variable. Keep $fakeProxy's temp path.

Error handling: a missing source must fail the run, never fall back to anything. Copying (rather than re-encoding with Set-Content) adds no BOM on Windows PowerShell 5.1.

Adjust ps1 scenario SETUPS for the unified knob semantics (for example, FAKE_SCOPE_* lists that relied on override). Do not touch their assertions about wrapper behaviour.

In docs/DEVELOPMENT.md (~line 218), say that both smoke tests run one shared fake proxy, scripts/tests/postflight-fake-proxy.js, which parity-check.sh and parity-check.ps1 enforce. Make the knob list match the shared file exactly, adding or removing names as harmonized.

Both parity checkers now pass.

Single verification gate on a fresh snapshot.

Snapshot: `git archive HEAD` with this task's six owned files overlaid byte-identically, on a native filesystem that Windows can reach, with MOE_*/CLAUDE* env scrubbed. Use the recipe from mem task-task-e92b2cb33f744bf18074fc87121f22df-handoff.

Evidence command, from the snapshot root: `bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh && MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180 bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh`. It must exit 0. Also required, each exiting 0 and recorded in the outputTail and summary with engine versions:
- parity-check.ps1 on Windows PowerShell 5.1 and on pwsh 7;
- postflight.ps1 with MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180 on Windows PowerShell 5.1 and on pwsh 7.

Timing: sh takes about 8.5 minutes and each ps1 engine about 11-13. Launch each run detached (setsid nohup writing a .log and a .done file) and poll in bounded loops under the 600 s tool cap. If a loaded box needs a larger timeout, record the value and the load as a deviation. Never silently retry a failure.

Coverage: each harness's printed frozen and commit-scope scenario counts must equal the counts in the latest landed dependency's recorded verification, or a baseline run if none is recorded. A drop means a scenario lost its knob.

RED proof (DoD 2), on a scratch copy of the snapshot:
1. Inject one difference: restore a private embedded proxy body in postflight.ps1.
2. Show that parity-check.sh and parity-check.ps1 both exit non-zero and name that harness.
3. Repeat for postflight.sh.
4. Restore.

planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 6 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 10 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
A (chosen): one shared fake proxy, scripts/tests/postflight-fake-proxy.js, copied by both harnesses. This follows the repo's mention-provenance precedent, where scripts/tests/mention-provenance-proxy.js is used by both mention-provenance.sh and .ps1. Drift between engines becomes impossible by construction, later rows edit one file instead of two, and the parity group only has to enforce that both harnesses install the shared file and neither re-embeds a private body.

B (rejected): keep two embedded copies, harmonize them hunk by hunk, and add an extract-and-compare checker. It meets DoD 2's literal example, but it keeps the duplication that caused the drift, and every future fake-proxy change would still have to be made twice.

Both approaches need the same per-hunk harmonization decisions; A needs no ongoing byte comparison. The description's 'for example' leaves the check's form open, and with A the 'injected difference' is a private body restored in one harness.

The frozen candidate suites are also embedded twice, but they are byte-identical (66055 B each, sha256 98683ba5…), so they are out of scope.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- Fake-proxy bodies at HEAD 1f9c7d5: sh 32732 B / 525 lines, ps1 31414 B / 508 lines, a 161-line diff in about 20 hunks. The full hunk list is in step 2.
- Both harnesses write the proxy to a temp path ($TMP_DIR/fake-proxy.js and $tempRoot\fake-proxy.js). The wrapper reaches it through MOE_PROXY_PATH, and the frozen suite gets it as argv.
- All six files are LF (.gitattributes `* text=auto eol=lf`).
- Knob usage counts (sh/ps1): FAKE_SCOPE_PEER_DECLARED 4/6, FAKE_SCOPE_PEERS_ACTIVE 7/13, FAKE_SCOPE_DECLARED_FIELD 5/6, FAKE_TASK_STATUS 38/18, FAKE_CLAIM_MODE 40/37. ps1 sets PEERS_ACTIVE although its get_commit_scope ignores it, so check where ps1 consumes it.
- Run times from e92b2cb3: postflight.sh about 8.5 min; postflight.ps1 about 11-13 min per engine.
- Both powershell.exe (5.1) and pwsh.exe are on the WSL PATH.
planningNotes.risks:
- Scenario semantics. Unifying FAKE_SCOPE_* (append vs override) and the BLOCKED-hold task id changes what one harness's scenarios see. Adjust setups, never wrapper assertions, and verify that scenario counts don't drop.
- Vacuous parity: match install lines, not mentions.
- Wrapper rail: never edit moe-agent.{sh,ps1}. A real wrapper difference that the union exposes becomes its own bug row, posted to #governors.
- PS 5.1: Copy-Item does not add a BOM, but records written with Set-Content still have one, so keep the BOM strip in readTask.
- Long runs: use detached runs and bounded polling. On a loaded box, record any timeout deviation.
- The dependencies (5f3960df, 07474ee4, c2cb5cf7) edit these bodies first. Re-measure and re-classify at the then-current HEAD; the architect's hunk list is a guide, not the contract.
- Never revert peers' dirty bytes.
